records.source: וַיָּ֕שָׁב הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י וַיְעִירֵ֕נִי כְּאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יֵע֥וֹר מִשְּׁנָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And returned the angel who talks with me and roused me, like a man who is roused from his sleep.
pieces: Then the angel who talked with me came back and woke me, as someone is woken from sleep.

L.1: And the angel who talked with me came back and roused me, like {{gender:a person|a man}} who is roused from {{gender:their|his}} sleep.

R.1: Then the angel who talked with me came back. He woke me up, the way someone is woken up from sleep.

decisions.choice: the fifth vision: a gold lampstand fed by two olive trees, with a word for Zerubbabel
decisions.reason: Zechariah sees a lampstand of gold with seven lamps, kept supplied with oil from two olive trees beside it (verses 2-3, 11-12). In the middle of the vision comes a word for Zerubbabel the governor: the temple will be finished not by human strength but by the LORD's Spirit (verses 6-10). The angel explains the seven lamps as the eyes of the LORD (verse 10) and the two trees as two anointed ones who stand beside the Lord of all the earth (verse 14).

decisions.choice: like someone roused from sleep: Zechariah is stirred to full attention
decisions.reason: The prophet is not said to have fallen asleep, but he was in a state like sleep, and the angel rouses him to see the next vision, as Daniel was roused in his visions (Daniel 8:18; 10:9-10). The angel "came back", as if he had stepped away after the last vision.

decisions.choice: a person / a man; their / his (L); someone (B, R)
decisions.reason: The comparison is with anyone woken from sleep, so Literal gives "a man ... his" the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "someone".

records.heading: The gold lampstand and the two olive trees

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֡ר רָאִ֣יתִי׀וְהִנֵּ֣ה מְנוֹרַת֩ זָהָ֨ב כֻּלָּ֜הּ וְגֻלָּ֣הּעַל־רֹאשָׁ֗הּ וְשִׁבְעָ֤ה נֵרֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ שִׁבְעָ֤ה וְשִׁבְעָה֙ מֽוּצָק֔וֹת לַנֵּר֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־רֹאשָֽׁהּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, What [are] you seeing? And I said, I see, and look, a lampstand of gold, all of it, and a bowl on its top, and its seven lamps on it, seven and seven pipes for the lamps which [are] on its top.
pieces: He asked me, "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a lampstand made entirely of gold, with a bowl at the top. There are seven lamps on it, and each of the lamps at the top has seven spouts.

L.2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see, and look, a lampstand all of gold, and a bowl on its top, and its seven lamps on it, seven and seven spouts for the lamps that [are] on its top.

R.2: He asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a lampstand made of solid gold, with a bowl at the top. It has seven lamps on it, and each lamp has seven places for wicks.

decisions.choice: and I said: the form the Hebrew text tells the reader to read
decisions.reason: The written letters of the Hebrew text have "and he said", and the form marked to be read aloud has "and I said". The reading form fits the dialogue: the angel asks, and Zechariah answers.

decisions.choice: a lampstand of gold with a bowl on top: a lampstand fed from an oil bowl above its lamps
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the seven-branched lampstand of the tabernacle (Exodus 25:31-40), which the priests kept supplied with oil (Exodus 27:20-21). This one is different: a bowl on top holds the oil and feeds the lamps, and the oil comes from two living olive trees (verse 3, 12), not from human hands. The word for bowl is used of a basin or a bowl-shaped lamp (Ecclesiastes 12:6).

decisions.choice: seven and seven spouts: seven spouts on each of the seven lamps
alternatives: seven pipes, one to each lamp
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "seven and seven", a way of saying "seven each". The word translated "spouts" is found only here; it seems to come from a verb for pouring, and may mean the pinched lips of a clay lamp where a wick lay, or pipes carrying oil from the bowl. Clay lamps with seven spouts around the rim have been found in the land of Israel. If so, the lampstand had seven lamps, each with seven flames. Others read seven pipes in all, one to each lamp.

decisions.choice: look (L); spouts (L, B); places for wicks (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order and "look". Balanced and Readable say "each of the lamps has seven", which is what "seven and seven" means (m3), and Readable says what a spout is for. Zechariah's description runs on into verse 3, where the quotation mark closes.

records.source: וּשְׁנַ֥יִם זֵיתִ֖ים עָלֶ֑יהָ אֶחָד֙ מִימִ֣ין הַגֻּלָּ֔ה וְאֶחָ֖ד עַל־שְׂמֹאלָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And two olive trees beside it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left.
pieces: And there are two olive trees beside it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left."

L.3: And two olive trees [are] beside it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left."

R.3: Beside it are two olive trees, one to the right of the bowl and one to the left."

decisions.choice: two olive trees: living sources of the oil for the lamps
decisions.reason: Lamps in Israel burned olive oil, and the tabernacle lamps were to be fed with pure oil of beaten olives (Exodus 27:20). Here the oil flows straight from the trees into the lampstand (verse 12), so the lamps never run dry and no one has to fill them. The angel explains the trees in verse 14.

decisions.choice: olive trees, at every level
decisions.reason: The picture is kept at every level, as set for the visions; the angel's own explanation comes at the end of the chapter.

records.source: וָאַ֨עַן֙ וָֽאֹמַ֔ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֛ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר מָה־אֵ֖לֶּה אֲדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I answered and said to the angel who talks with me, saying, What [are] these, my lord?
pieces: I asked the angel who talked with me, "My lord, what are these?"

L.4: And I answered and said to the angel who talked with me, "What [are] these, my lord?"

R.4: I asked the angel who talked with me, "My lord, what are these things?"

decisions.choice: what are these: the things Zechariah has just seen
decisions.reason: "These" may be the whole lampstand with its trees, or the two olive trees, which Zechariah asks about again in verses 11-12. The angel's full answer comes only in verses 10 and 14.

decisions.choice: My lord, what are these? (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the polite address first, as English speakers do. "My lord" is lowercase, as in 1:9.

records.source: וַ֠יַּעַן הַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּי֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הֲל֥וֹא יָדַ֖עְתָּ מָה־הֵ֣מָּה אֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֖ר לֹ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And answered the angel who talks with me and said to me, Do not you know what these [are]? And I said, No, my lord.
pieces: The angel who talked with me answered, "Do you not know what these are?" "No, my lord," I replied.

L.5: And the angel who talked with me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."

R.5: The angel who talked with me asked, "Do you not know what these are?" "No, my lord," I answered.

decisions.choice: do you not know: a question that prepares for the answer, not a rebuke
decisions.reason: The angel asks the same question again in verse 13. It makes the prophet, and the reader, admit that the meaning cannot be guessed and must be given.

decisions.choice: "No, my lord," I replied (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the short answer first and the speaker after it, as English dialogue often does.

records.source: וַיַּ֜עַן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֚ה דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א בְחַ֨יִל֙ וְלֹ֣א בְכֹ֔חַ כִּ֣י אִם־בְּרוּחִ֔י אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And he answered and said to me, saying, This [is the] word of Yahweh to Zerubbabel, saying: Not by might, and not by power, but by my Spirit, says Yahweh of hosts.
pieces: Then he told me, "Here is the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for Zerubbabel: 'Not by might, nor by power, but by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.6: And he answered and said to me, saying, "This [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s word to Zerubbabel: 'Not by might, nor by power, but by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.

R.6: So he told me, "This is a message for Zerubbabel from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Not by might, nor by power, but by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: a word for Zerubbabel inside the vision
alternatives: a passage moved here from elsewhere
decisions.reason: Instead of explaining the lampstand at once, the angel gives a word for Zerubbabel, which runs to the middle of verse 10; then the explanation resumes. Some think these verses once stood elsewhere, but as the text stands the word explains the vision: as the lamps burn with oil that no human hand supplies, the temple will be finished by the LORD's Spirit, not by human strength.

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel: governor of Judah and heir of David's line
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel was governor of Judah under the Persians (Haggai 1:1) and led the first group of exiles home with Joshua (Ezra 2:2; 3:2). He was a grandson of King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:17-19), so he was of the royal family of David. Haggai calls him the LORD's chosen signet ring (Haggai 2:23). With Joshua he led the rebuilding of the temple.

decisions.choice: might ... power: any human strength, whether armies, wealth or effort
decisions.reason: The first word means strength or ability, and is used for armies and for wealth (Exodus 14:4; Deuteronomy 8:17-18). The second means strength or power in general. Together they rule out every human resource as the means by which the work will be done.

decisions.choice: by my Spirit: by the LORD's own power at work
decisions.reason: The word means wind, breath or spirit, and here it is the LORD's Spirit: his power at work among his people. Haggai 2:5 had promised, "My Spirit remains among you; do not fear." Like the oil that flows to the lamps from the living trees, the Spirit supplies what the builders cannot.

decisions.choice: Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, at every level
decisions.reason: The saying keeps one wording at every level, as set for this verse, because readers know it and quote it. "Spirit" is capitalized for God's Spirit, as in Isaiah. The angel's words are in double quotation marks, and the word to Zerubbabel is in single marks inside them; both close at the end of verse 7.

records.source: מִֽי־אַתָּ֧ה הַֽר־הַגָּד֛וֹל לִפְנֵ֥י זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל לְמִישֹׁ֑ר וְהוֹצִיא֙ אֶת־הָאֶ֣בֶן הָרֹאשָׁ֔ה תְּשֻׁא֕וֹת חֵ֥ן חֵ֖ן לָֽהּ׃פ
records.gloss: Who [are] you, O mountain the great? Before Zerubbabel [you will become] a plain. And he will bring out the stone the top, shoutings, Grace, grace to it!
pieces: What are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become level ground. He will bring out the top stone while people shout, "Grace, grace to it!"'"

L.7: Who [are] you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel [you will become] a plain! And he will bring out the top stone amid shouts of "Grace, grace to it!"'"

R.7: Great mountain, who do you think you are? Before Zerubbabel you will become flat ground. He will bring out the last stone of the temple while the people shout, "God bless it! God bless it!"'"

decisions.choice: the great mountain will become a plain: every obstacle to the rebuilding will be removed
decisions.reason: The mountain stands for whatever stood in Zerubbabel's way. It may be the opposition of the peoples around, which had stopped the work for years (Ezra 4:1-5, 24; 5:3-5), or the great heap of rubble on the temple site, or the sheer size of the task. The text does not say. The picture of mountains made level is used of the LORD's coming in Isaiah 40:4.

decisions.choice: the top stone: the last stone, which marks the building complete
alternatives: the first stone, laid at the start of the building
decisions.reason: The word comes from "head", which can mean the top of something or its first or chief part. If the top stone is meant, Zerubbabel will set the last stone and so complete the temple, as verse 9 says he will finish it. Some read it as the first or chief stone, set when the work began again. The text does not describe the stone more closely.

decisions.choice: Grace, grace to it!: a shout calling down God's favor on the stone
alternatives: How beautiful, how beautiful it is!
decisions.reason: The word means favor or grace, and also charm or beauty. The people's shout may be a blessing on the finished building, asking for God's favor on it, or a cry of delight at its beauty. The first sense fits the theme of the chapter, that the work is done by God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: who do you think you are? (R); the last stone of the temple (R); God bless it! (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a challenge, which is how it is meant, and says which stone is meant and what the shout asks for (m3). "Grace, grace" would mean little to a new reader. The closing marks end the word to Zerubbabel and the angel's words.

records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.8: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.8: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: a second word about Zerubbabel
decisions.reason: The formula introduces a word given to Zechariah himself, which goes on from verses 6-7: Zerubbabel, who began the temple, will finish it. The message is not in quotation marks, as the prophets' messages are not.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording set for the prophets at each level.

records.heading: Zerubbabel will finish the house

records.source: יְדֵ֣י זְרֻבָּבֶ֗ל יִסְּד֛וּ הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה וְיָדָ֣יו תְּבַצַּ֑עְנָה וְיָ֣דַעְתָּ֔ כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: [The] hands of Zerubbabel have founded the house this, and his hands will finish [it]; and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me to you.
pieces: Zerubbabel's hands have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will bring it to completion. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.

L.9: The hands of Zerubbabel have founded this house, and his hands will finish [it]; and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me to you.

R.9: Zerubbabel has laid the foundation of this temple with his own hands, and with his own hands he will finish it. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.

decisions.choice: founded this house: began building the temple
decisions.reason: Ezra 3:8-10 tells of the foundation laid under Zerubbabel and Jeshua soon after the return, and Haggai 2:18 dates the founding of the temple to the year of this prophecy, 520 BC, when the stalled work began again. The verb can mean the start of the building as a whole. The temple was finished in the sixth year of Darius, 515 BC (Ezra 6:14-15).

decisions.choice: you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me: the finished temple will prove the message true
decisions.reason: The words are the same as in 2:13 and 2:15. When Zerubbabel completes the temple, the people will know that the prophet spoke for the LORD (Deuteronomy 18:21-22). "You" is singular here, perhaps speaking to Zechariah, perhaps to each hearer.

decisions.choice: temple (R); with his own hands (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "house" and makes the point of "his hands" plain: the man who began the work will finish it himself. Literal says "you shall know", as in 2:13 and 2:15.

records.source: כִּ֣י מִ֣י בַז֮ לְי֣וֹם קְטַנּוֹת֒ וְשָׂמְח֗וּ וְרָא֞וּ אֶת־הָאֶ֧בֶן הַבְּדִ֛יל בְּיַ֥ד זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל שִׁבְעָה־אֵ֑לֶּה עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הֵ֥מָּה מְשׁוֹטְטִ֖ים בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: For who has despised [the] day of small things? And they will rejoice and see the stone the tin in [the] hand of Zerubbabel. These seven [are] the eyes of Yahweh; they range in all the earth.
pieces: Who has despised the day of small beginnings? People will rejoice when they see the plumb stone in Zerubbabel's hand. These seven are the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which range over the whole earth.

L.10: For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven [are] the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; they range through all the earth.

R.10: Some people looked down on the work because it began so small. But they will be glad when they see Zerubbabel holding the plumb stone. These seven lamps are the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which look over the whole earth.

decisions.choice: the day of small things: a time of small beginnings
decisions.reason: The new temple seemed nothing compared with Solomon's (Haggai 2:3), and older people who had seen the first temple wept when its foundation was laid (Ezra 3:12). The question rebukes those who looked down on the work because it was small.

decisions.choice: they will rejoice: those who despised the small beginnings will rejoice when they see the work going on
alternatives: these seven, the eyes of the LORD, will rejoice when they see the stone in Zerubbabel's hand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be divided in two ways. The verbs "rejoice" and "see" may have as their subject the people who despised the work: they will change their minds. Or "these seven" may be the subject: the LORD's eyes will see the work with joy. The main division of the Hebrew falls after "Zerubbabel", which favors the first reading.

decisions.choice: the tin stone: a builder's plumb weight
alternatives: an inscribed tin or lead tablet for the foundation
decisions.reason: The second word usually means tin (Numbers 31:22; Ezekiel 22:18), so the phrase is "the stone, the tin". It is most often read as a plumb weight of tin or lead hanging from a line, used to check that a wall is straight. Zerubbabel holding it means that he is in charge of the building. The same letters can mean "separation" or "chosen", and some read a stone set apart for the building, or a metal tablet laid in the foundation.

decisions.choice: these seven are the eyes of the LORD: the seven lamps show God's watchful care over all the earth
decisions.reason: "These seven" are the seven lamps of verse 2. The angel explains them as the LORD's eyes, which see everything. 2 Chronicles 16:9 says the same: "the eyes of the LORD range throughout the whole earth to strengthen those whose heart is true to him". The seven eyes on the stone in 3:9 seem to be the same.

decisions.choice: Some people looked down on the work because it began so small (R); These seven lamps (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a plain statement of what it means and says "lamps", since "these seven" points back to the seven lamps. Balanced says "plumb stone" for the tin stone (m3), and Literal keeps the Hebrew word.

records.source: וָאַ֖עַן וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְּׁנֵ֤י הַזֵּיתִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶה עַל־יְמִ֥ין הַמְּנוֹרָ֖ה וְעַל־שְׂמֹאולָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And I answered and said to him, What [are] the two olive trees the these on the right of the lampstand and on its left?
pieces: Then I asked him, "What are these two olive trees to the right and left of the lampstand?"

L.11: And I answered and said to him, "What [are] these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"

R.11: Then I asked the angel, "What are these two olive trees, one on the right side of the lampstand and one on the left?"

decisions.choice: Zechariah asks again: the vision resumes
decisions.reason: The angel has explained the seven lamps, but not the trees. Zechariah asks about them twice (verses 11 and 12), the second time more precisely.

decisions.choice: the angel (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the angel for "him", since the word to Zerubbabel has come between.

records.source: וָאַ֣עַן שֵׁנִ֔ית וָאֹמַ֖ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְׁתֵּ֞י שִׁבֲּלֵ֣י הַזֵּיתִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּיַ֗ד שְׁנֵי֙ צַנְתְּר֣וֹת הַזָּהָ֔ב הַֽמְרִיקִ֥ים מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַזָּהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And I answered a second [time] and said to him, What [are the] two branches of the olive trees which [are] beside [the] two pipes of the gold, which empty out from them the gold?
pieces: I asked him again, "What are the two branches of the olive trees beside the two gold pipes that pour out the golden oil?"

L.12: And I answered a second time and said to him, "What [are] the two branches of the olive trees that [are] beside the two golden pipes, which pour out from themselves the gold?"

R.12: I asked him again, "What are the two olive branches beside the two gold pipes? Golden oil is pouring out through them."

decisions.choice: branches: olive branches heavy with fruit
decisions.reason: The word usually means an ear of grain (Genesis 41:5). Here it is used of the olive trees, so it seems to mean a fruit-laden branch or cluster from which the oil comes.

decisions.choice: pipes: channels carrying oil from the trees to the lampstand
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It seems to mean a pipe or channel, perhaps the spouts of a press. The picture is of oil flowing from the trees, through gold pipes, into the bowl of the lampstand, without any human hand.

decisions.choice: the gold: the golden oil
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that the pipes "pour out the gold". Fresh olive oil is golden in color, and the word is used for the oil that is golden like the lampstand.

decisions.choice: the golden oil (B); Golden oil (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "oil", which the context makes plain (m3). Readable splits the question into a question and a statement.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא יָדַ֖עְתָּ מָה־אֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֖ר לֹ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, saying, Do not you know what these [are]? And I said, No, my lord.
pieces: He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" "No, my lord," I answered.

L.13: And he said to me, "Do you not know what these [are]?" And I said, "No, my lord."

R.13: He said, "Do you not know what these are?" "No, my lord," I answered.

decisions.choice: do you not know: the question of verse 5 again
decisions.reason: The angel repeats his question, and Zechariah repeats his answer. The repetition slows the scene before the final explanation.

records.gloss: And he said, These [are the] two sons of the fresh oil who stand by [the] Lord of all the earth.
pieces: So he said, "These are the two anointed ones who stand beside the Lord of all the earth."

L.14: And he said, "These [are] the two sons of fresh oil who stand by the Lord of all the earth."

R.14: So he said, "These are the two who have been anointed with oil to serve the Lord of the whole earth. They stand in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence."

decisions.choice: the two sons of fresh oil: two people set apart by anointing
alternatives: two who are full of oil
decisions.reason: "Son of" a thing means one who belongs to it or is marked by it. Kings and priests were anointed with oil when they took office (Exodus 29:7; 1 Samuel 16:13), so "sons of oil" are most likely two anointed leaders. The word here is the one for fresh oil, not the usual word for anointing oil, so some read "the two who supply oil". The angel does not name them. In the book's setting they are most often taken as Joshua the high priest and Zerubbabel, the heir of David, the two leaders named in chapters 3 and 4; together they serve the LORD as his chosen leaders.

decisions.choice: the Lord of all the earth: God as ruler of the whole world
decisions.reason: The title is used of God in Joshua 3:11, 13, Micah 4:13 and Psalm 97:5. It fits the visions, in which the LORD's eyes and riders go through all the earth.

decisions.choice: Revelation 11:4: the two witnesses are "the two olive trees and the two lampstands"
decisions.reason: Revelation takes up this vision for the two witnesses who prophesy in the last days and stand "before the Lord of the earth".

decisions.choice: sons of fresh oil (L); anointed ones (B); who have been anointed with oil (R); Lord, capitalized
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew expression; Balanced and Readable give its likely sense (m1). The Lord here is God, so the word is capitalized, as set for the word "lord" used of God, and Readable's "his" takes the setting for pronouns of God.
